resolution: Pinned directory handles and no-follow reads/atomic writes; Windows denies directory write/delete sharing, including junction mutation. Audio decodes bytes read through the same boundary.
SAX preflight budgets before project, package-manifest and GLB DOM allocation; aggregate decoded-image budget. These are conservative estimates, not a custom allocator.
Uncooperative mesh and GLB export work runs in deadline-killed child processes with native CPU limits, Windows/Linux memory limits and a best-effort macOS data limit.
No silent 4096-event truncation. Explicit 32768 actor/zone pair budget prevents Play or pauses a changed runtime.
Complete overlap state within the pair budget; tested with 10000 simultaneous overlaps and exits.
Scene snapshots include script source, language, module metadata and open state; code editor also has bounded text undo.
Oversized history states produce a visible warning; history is bounded to 128 MiB and 64 states.
Completed scene operations request a checkpoint; configurable 1–60-second recovery defaults to five seconds, including during Play.
Texture cache has a 128 MiB budget and a 256-entry LRU bound.
Container writing and CRC validation stream bounded chunks; resource deduplication uses hashes plus byte comparison, without duplicate vector map keys.
History accounts for game icon storage and script sources; oversized snapshots are reported.
A spatial grid replaces all-pairs candidate discovery; legacy collision-response differential fixtures remain covered. Dense overlapping worlds can still be costly.
Swept static collision stops a fast mover at a thin wall. This is AABB physics, not a general rigid-body CCD solver.
No Authenticode publisher certificate is available. Windows is unsigned; macOS has an explicit ad-hoc signature, not Developer ID notarization.
Dependency inventory, binary hashes, pinned NuGet lock and current .NET security runtime are recorded. An inventory/advisory lookup cannot prove every vendored dependency vulnerability-free.
Deterministic mutation/load/undo soak and a scheduled one-hour project-parser endurance workflow are supplied. No claim of completed exhaustive or coverage-guided format fuzzing.

CRC32 detects accidental corruption only. Download authenticity relies on the release origin and build provenance; archives carry SHA-256 inventories. Local modified game containers are not authenticated.
MCP defaults to read-only. Mutations require --allow-write; Lua additionally requires --allow-lua. Hidden calls are also denied and audited.
A swept pass-through emits enter and exit during the same simulation tick. This deliberate edge contract is tested.
Executable permission changes use the still-open output descriptor; failure removes the anchored temporary output. Rename failure also cleans up.
Schema/format 3 explicitly reads schemas 1–3 and creates a pre-migration backup. Older engine versions cannot be expected to read schema 3.
Luaryx entities and C# Entity objects retain stable IDs across removals. Legacy index APIs remain for compatibility.
Luaryx.find and C# Scene.Find reject duplicate names; use stable IDs. Legacy find_object still returns its historical first match.
Join rejects animated, textured, procedural, controller or custom-property inputs instead of silently discarding their data. Character generation creates a new object.
Play recovery serializes the saved edit world with current script source, never the disposable simulated positions.
Texture keys include file identity, size and write timestamp (or embedded content hash), and texture generations invalidate cached bindings.
Cache admission preserves the active geometry working set; oversubscribed meshes use the immediate renderer rather than evicting and re-uploading visible entries every frame.
Audio uses bounded encoded-byte reads and streaming decoders; aggregate backend encoded data is limited to 64 MiB. Document/undo copies remain bounded by their own budgets.
Record observed RSS/descriptors during the 1000-cycle soak and sanitizer checks. These do not prove leak freedom for hour-long GPU sessions on every driver.
GLB JSON is preflighted before tinygltf DOM creation; decoded images have an aggregate budget in addition to dimension/file/scene limits.
Spatial queries find trigger candidates; kill/checkpoint processing reuses touched zone IDs instead of scanning all zones for each actor.
Simulation keeps up to two seconds of backlog and exposes any further dropped time in the debugger. It does not silently throw away every heavy frame remainder.
UI GLB export captures a scene snapshot and runs a bounded worker exchange asynchronously, with completion reported on the UI thread.
Windows long-path-aware manifest and extended-length absolute Unicode file paths are enabled. Individual document/path field limits still apply.
Static GLB import/export is supported; ignored animation/skinning/extensions are reported. Full glTF animation/skinning interoperability is not advertised.
Container bounds are now 4096 entries and 1 GiB payload, including the required C# runtime; limits are explicit, not unlimited.
Tests cover named regressions, native platforms, sanitizer checks, a mutation soak and actual UI input. Finite checks are not proof of all race conditions or leaks being absent.
Native Windows/macOS and Linux software-OpenGL checks are required. No claim covers every GPU model, operating-system version or third-party driver.
Project owner selected GPL-3.0; LICENSE, NOTICE and contribution terms are present. Third-party licenses and platform trademarks retain their terms.
Release publication consumes the successful immutable CI run, tested native artifacts, video evidence, hashes and provenance; exactly four uploaded release assets.
